*Adjusts spectacles and surveys the tempestuous requirements before me*

By my so potent art, I shall bring order to this chaos! Though the Product Manager is swept away in the storms of meetings, we must chart our course through these uncertain waters.

Let me first conjure the questions that hang unanswered in the air...

## Questions for the Product Manager (Currently Unanswered)

*Strokes beard thoughtfully*

**On the Nature of Notifications:**
1. What events shall trigger these notifications? (Comments, mentions, updates, approvals?)
2. Through what channels must our messages flow? (Email, in-app, push, SMS?)
3. Can users control their notification preferences, or shall we decide for them?
4. What is the urgency? Must notifications arrive in real-time, or can they wait?
5. Should notifications be grouped or arrive individually?

**On the Technical Realm:**
6. Do we have budget for third-party services (SendGrid, Twilio, etc.)?
7. What is our data retention policy for notification history?
8. Are there compliance considerations (GDPR, email opt-out requirements)?

**On Priorities and Scope:**
9. Which user segments receive these powers first?
10. What is "important" - all events, or curated ones?

## Reasonable Assumptions (By My Art)

Since the PM is detained, I shall make these judgments:

- **Primary channel:** Email (users already have addresses)
- **Secondary channel:** In-app notifications (visible when logged in)
- **User control:** Users can manage their preferences
- **Events:** Comments on their items, @mentions, status changes on watched items
- **Real-time:** Near real-time for in-app, batched for email (avoid spam)
- **No third-party budget initially:** Build simple, prove value first
- **Data retention:** 30 days of notification history
- **Scope:** Web first, then mobile

## Epic Breakdown: User Notifications

*Waves staff to organize the stories in proper sequence*

### Story 1: Notification Data Model & Storage
**As a** developer  
**I want** a database schema for storing notifications  
**So that** we can persist and query notification data

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Notifications table includes: id, user_id, event_type, content, read_status, created_at
- Index on user_id and created_at for efficient queries
- Migration script runs cleanly on test environment
- Can store at least 10,000 notifications per user without performance degradation
- Automated cleanup of notifications older than 30 days

**Story Points:** 3  
**Dependencies:** None (foundational)  
**Technical Enabler:** Yes

---

### Story 2: In-App Notification Display
**As a** user  
**I want** to see a notification bell icon with a count of unread notifications  
**So that** I know when something requires my attention

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Bell icon appears in application header on all pages
- Badge shows count of unread notifications (up to 99+)
- Clicking bell opens dropdown showing last 10 notifications
- Each notification shows: message, timestamp, read/unread indicator
- Clicking a notification marks it as read and navigates to related content

**Story Points:** 5  
**Dependencies:** Story 1 (requires notification data model)

---

### Story 3: Notification Generation for Comments
**As a** user  
**I want** to be notified when someone comments on my content  
**So that** I can respond to feedback quickly

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- New comment on user's item creates notification record
- Notification includes: commenter name, preview of comment (first 50 chars), link to item
- Notification appears in user's in-app feed within 5 seconds
- User who made the comment does NOT receive notification
- Batch job prevents duplicate notifications for same event

**Story Points:** 5  
**Dependencies:** Stories 1 & 2

---

### Story 4: @Mention Notifications
**As a** user  
**I want** to be notified when someone @mentions me  
**So that** I don't miss important call-outs

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Comments with @username pattern trigger notification
- Notification includes: who mentioned them, context (first 100 chars), link to comment
- Only valid usernames trigger notifications (username validation)
- User sees "You were mentioned" notification type clearly differentiated
- Works in comments, descriptions, and any rich text field

**Story Points:** 3  
**Dependencies:** Story 3 (extends comment notifications)

---

### Story 5: Notification Preferences Management
**As a** user  
**I want** to control which notifications I receive  
**So that** I'm not overwhelmed with irrelevant updates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- New "Notification Settings" page accessible from user profile
- Toggle switches for each notification type (comments, mentions, status changes)
- Email frequency setting: Real-time, Daily digest, Weekly digest, Never
- Changes save immediately with success confirmation
- Preferences persist across sessions and devices

**Story Points:** 5  
**Dependencies:** Stories 2, 3, 4 (need notification types to exist)

---

### Story 6: Email Notification Service
**As a** user  
**I want** to receive email notifications for important events  
**So that** I stay informed even when not logged in

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Background job processes notification queue every 5 minutes
- Respects user email preferences (frequency, opt-out)
- Email template includes: clear subject line, notification content, CTA link to app
- Unsubscribe link in email footer
- Email sending errors logged but don't block notification creation

**Story Points:** 8  
**Dependencies:** Story 5 (requires preference system)  
**Technical Enabler:** Yes (email infrastructure)

---

### Story 7: Notification History View
**As a** user  
**I want** to view all my past notifications  
**So that** I can review what I might have missed

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- "View All Notifications" link from bell dropdown
- Full page shows paginated list of all notifications (20 per page)
- Filter by: Read/Unread, Notification Type, Date Range
- Mark all as read button
- Delete notification option (soft delete, not in database)

**Story Points:** 5  
**Dependencies:** Story 2 (extends in-app notifications)

---

### Story 8: Status Change Notifications
**As a** user  
**I want** to be notified when items I'm watching change status  
**So that** I can track progress on things that matter to me

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Users can "watch" items (new watch/unwatch toggle)
- Status changes on watched items create notifications
- Notification shows: item name, old status → new status, who changed it
- Bulk status changes don't spam (max 1 notification per user per batch operation)
- Unwatching an item stops future notifications

**Story Points:** 5  
**Dependencies:** Stories 1 & 2

---

## Implementation Priority & Sprint Planning

*Arranges the scrolls in order of conjuring*

**Sprint 1 (Capacity: 20 points)** - Foundation
- Story 1: Data Model (3 pts) - MUST GO FIRST
- Story 2: In-App Display (5 pts) - Core UI
- Story 3: Comment Notifications (5 pts) - First real notification
- Story 4: @Mentions (3 pts) - Quick win
- Buffer: 4 points for unexpected complexity

**Sprint 2 (Capacity: 20 points)** - Preferences & Email
- Story 5: Preferences (5 pts) - User control
- Story 6: Email Service (8 pts) - Major technical lift
- Story 7: History View (5 pts) - Complete the in-app experience
- Buffer: 2 points

**Sprint 3 (If needed)**
- Story 8: Status Changes (5 pts) - Additional notification type
- Hardening, monitoring, documentation

## Technical Risks & Mitigations

*Warns of storms ahead*

**Risk:** Email deliverability and spam filters  
**Mitigation:** Start with transactional email provider trial, implement SPF/DKIM

**Risk:** Notification overload causing user frustration  
**Mitigation:** Story 5 (preferences) in Sprint 2, not deferred

**Risk:** Performance with high notification volume  
**Mitigation:** Story 1 includes indexing, background job processing in Story 6

---

We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and this epic shall take shape through two sprints of careful orchestration. The foundation in Sprint 1 allows parallel work in Sprint 2, with the email infrastructure as our most complex conjuring.

*Taps staff on ground*

Now my charms are all o'erthrown - the chaos is ordered, and the team may proceed with confidence! Though the PM is absent, we have charted a course through reasonable assumptions and clear priorities.

What say you? Shall we begin this tempest of development? 🎭⚡
